So, as I've mentioned a few times on here, I've been on a calorie-restricted diet for a while. Went from 167 (at 5'8, I was a singular pound into the overweight range..) to 152, and lost my motivation and quit there while my goal weight was 135. I had a bunch of non-scale goals I've been going for as well, but with a cross-country move, new job start, and all the stress that came with that, I stopped for a bit and have just been maintaining.

That is until I visited my grandfather.

We lost my grandmother a bit over a year ago. She had stage 4 cancer, and didn't know it until she caught pneumonia and was getting that treated. She was gone in less than two weeks. My grandfather was understandably devastated. I figured a visit from his favorite granddaughter might cheer him up for a bit, so I went down for the weekend. I was honestly scared back to dieting by what I saw.

He has always been a big man, but he told me he had gained 30 pounds in the last year. (At 5'7, he's probably bordering on 250.) As a result, he was getting less and less mobile. He can only use tables at restaurants because he can't get out of the booths. It takes four or five tries for him to swing his leg up so he can climb into his car. And he admitted to me that all he does is eat, because it hurts to move, because he's putting on weight.

We went to one of his favorite bars (my grandpa likes to drink me under the table when I visit), and another regular couple there were in their 90's. They were slim, fit, went golfing every day, and the man told my grandpa he deserved the beer he was having because he 'woke up, had breakfast, had another rest, and then went out and worked in the yard all day." My grandfather just shook his head and tried to get off of his stool, which took a few minutes.

If you take care of yourself, you can do so much more with your life. One of the reasons he's suffering is because he can't do anything due to complications of his weight. I've been scared back to dieting because I don't ever want to get old and immobile just because I have some extra weight. I want to be the 90 year old woman going golfing at least 6 holes a day, just as fit as I am now at 25. I don't want to turn into an old age ham who can hardly get out of their chair. And I hope some other shitlord or shitlady out there finds this as motivation to continue their fitness journey, as well. Take care of yourselves.
